headline: Returns to profit, but revenue and occupancy keep softening
summary_short: Kilroy's Q2 FY2026 revenue fell 6% y/y to $272.4 million and Net Operating Income dropped 5.5% to $180.3 million as stabilized occupancy slid to 77.0% from 81.6% at year-end; diluted EPS returned to a $0.17 profit after Q1's impairment-driven $0.16 loss but stayed down 70% from $0.57 a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue fell 6% y/y to $272.4M and NOI fell 5.5% to $180.3M, mainly from 2025-2026 property dispositions and a redevelopment property that stopped capitalizing interest after stabilizing, partly offset by recent acquisitions. Interest expense rose 35% y/y to $41.6M on that same lost capitalization. FFO fell 19.5% y/y to $109.3M. Diluted EPS was $0.17, down 70% y/y from $0.57 but up from Q1's $0.16 loss, which included a $61.8M impairment not repeated this quarter. Stabilized occupancy fell to 77.0% from 81.6% at year-end. Share repurchases paused after $72.7M in Q1. Cash rose to $253.8M, largely on $330.3M of disposition proceeds. No forward guidance was issued in this filing.

drivers.explanation: NOI fell $10.5M y/y as $12.8M lost from disposed properties and $4.0M from a redevelopment property that stopped capitalizing interest after stabilizing outweighed a $6.2M gain from acquisitions and a $0.2M same-property gain.

Lower NOI combined with a $10.8M (35%) rise in interest expense, driven by the cessation of capitalized interest on a redevelopment property that stabilized in Q1 2026, and the absence of a $16.6M prior-year gain on property sales.
Tracks the same NOI decline and higher interest expense described above; the release does not itemize FFO drivers separately from the net income and NOI reconciliations.
Q1 FY2026 included a $61.8M impairment charge on real estate assets with none recurring in Q2, explaining the swing from a per-share loss to a per-share profit quarter over quarter.

Stabilized portfolio occupancy fell to 77.0% from 81.6% at year-end 2025 as a newly stabilized life-science property (7% occupied) entered the pool; share repurchases paused in Q2 after $72.7M bought back in Q1.
